questions.question_text: The part of hypothalamus that acts as a satiety centre is
questions.explanation: Ventromedial hypothalamus acts as a satiety centre; lateral hypothalamus as a feeding centre. In animals with a lesion of the ventromedial hypothalamus, abnormal feeding behaviours including hyperphagia that leads to obesity are noted.

questions.question_text: What proportion (in percentage) of the brain is occupied by prefrontal cortex?
questions.explanation: The prefrontal cortex (PFC) occupies nearly 30% of the brain.

questions.question_text: In what percentage of left-handed people the left hemisphere is dominant?
questions.explanation: In left-handed people, 64% have left hemisphere dominance, with 20% right hemisphere dominant, and 16% showing bilateral dominance.

questions.question_text: Cranial nerves can carry both sensory and motor impulses. Which one of the following cranial nerves has only a motor component?
questions.explanation: Pure motor cranial nerves include Oculomotor, trochlear, abducens, accessory, and hypoglossal nerves.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following effects is associated with lesions of the left hemisphere?
questions.explanation: Left hemisphere lesions may produce alexia, agraphia, and other language-related issues.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following types of neurons has no axons?
questions.explanation: Amacrine neurons are characterized by their lack of axons.

questions.question_text: Nominal aphasia can be localised to
questions.explanation: Posterior lesions involving parietal cortex, particularly of the angular gyrus, can produce pronounced anomia.

questions.question_text: Which area of the brain is responsible for normal arithmetical ability?
questions.explanation: The angular gyrus is involved in cognitive processes related to numbers and language.

questions.question_text: Which artery supplies most of the corpus callosum?
questions.explanation: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the majority of the corpus callosum.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cells are the largest of all neurons in the human brain?
questions.explanation: Betz cells are large pyramidal neurons found in the primary motor cortex.

questions.question_text: A lesion affecting which of the following structures can cause dysarthria?
questions.explanation: Dysarthria occurs due to upper motor neuron lesions affecting the motor functions related to speech.

questions.question_text: The internal capsule is supplied by which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The internal capsule receives blood supply from various branches of the Circle of Willis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is affected if there is an occlusion of the posterior cerebral artery?
questions.explanation: The posterior cerebral artery supplies the dentate gyrus and various areas of the hippocampal formation.

questions.question_text: The thalamus and hypothalamus are constituents of which of the following embryological structures?
questions.explanation: The thalamus and hypothalamus develop from the diencephalon in embryogenesis.

questions.question_text: Mrs. X is an 83-year-old lady who has been diagnosed with early stages of Alzheimer's disease. The brain region, which could show prominent changes, is;
questions.explanation: Significant loss of entorhinal cortex neurons occurs in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: Synaptogenesis is at its highest during which of the following phases of life?
questions.explanation: The peak of synaptogenesis occurs within the first two postnatal years.

questions.question_text: Mr. Y developed normal pressure hydrocephalus following trauma in the basal brain. The obstruction is most likely to have occurred in the;
questions.explanation: The commonest site of block in non-communicating hydrocephalus is foramen of Munro.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a function of astrocytes?
questions.explanation: Formation of CNS myelin sheath is a function of oligodendrocytes, not astrocytes.

questions.question_text: Obstruction to CSF circulation leads to non-communicating hydrocephalus. The cerebrospinal fluid passes into the subarachnoid space via recesses in which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: CSF passes into the subarachnoid space via recesses in the fourth ventricle.

questions.question_text: A 62-year-old gentleman presented to the outpatients department with a history of changes in personality, socially disinhibited behaviour, poor judgement and irritability. His carer also reported a recent history of urinary incontinence. Which part of the brain is most likely to be affected?
questions.explanation: Frontal lobe dysfunction can present with changes in personality and social behaviour.

questions.question_text: Forced utilization behaviour can be a feature of damage to which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: Damage to the orbitofrontal cortex can lead to forced utilization behaviour where individuals may use objects placed before them.

questions.question_text: Which of the following enzymes is exclusively seen in astrocytes?
questions.explanation: Glutamate dehydrogenase is an enzyme that is uniquely present in astrocytes.

questions.question_text: Lesions in the subthalamic area are associated with which of the following movement disorders?
questions.explanation: Lesions in the subthalamic nucleus are linked with hemiballismus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a part of Papez circuit?
questions.explanation: Heschl's gyrus is involved in auditory processing and not part of the Papez circuit.

questions.question_text: The limbic Papez circuit includes which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The Papez circuit includes the hippocampus along with structures like the fornix and cingulate gyrus.

questions.question_text: In which area of the brain is the dentate gyrus located?
questions.explanation: The dentate gyrus is part of the hippocampal formation, which is involved in memory formation and neurogenesis.

questions.question_text: Mirror neurons are found in which part of the brain?
questions.explanation: Mirror neurons are believed to be present in the inferior frontal cortex and superior parietal cortices, involved in action understanding and imitation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about microglia is correct?

options.text: It is mainly responsible for myelination
It is present outside brain and spinal cord
It constitutes 70% of glial population in brain
It is sensitive to sodium channel stimulation

questions.explanation: Microglial cells are derived from the mesoderm, unlike neurons and other glial cells which come from the neuroectoderm.

questions.question_text: Which function of the brain is served by angular gyrus?
questions.explanation: The angular gyrus is involved in the processing of language, especially in reading and writing.

questions.question_text: Foramina of Munro are channels that connect
questions.explanation: The foramina of Monro connect the two lateral ventricles with the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following structures is involved in the visual pathway?
questions.explanation: The lateral geniculate body is part of the thalamus and is a primary relay center for visual information.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures divide the frontal lobe from the temporal lobe?
questions.explanation: The lateral sulcus, also known as the Sylvian fissure, separates the frontal lobe from the temporal lobe.

questions.question_text: The foramen of Monro connects

options.text: Fourth ventricle to central canal of spinal cord

questions.explanation: The foramen of Monro, also known as the interventricular foramen, connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding amygdala is NOT correct?

options.text: Learning does not occur in the absence of memory consolidation mediated by amygdala
Emotional face processing involves amygdalar activity
It is involved in emotional memory
Damage leads to impaired fear conditioning
Monkeys with amygdalar damage show impaired maternal behaviours

correct_answer.text: Learning does not occur in the absence of memory consolidation mediated by amygdala

correct_answers.text: Learning does not occur in the absence of memory consolidation mediated by amygdala

questions.explanation: Learning and memory can still occur without the amygdala, especially if emotional arousal is not involved.

questions.question_text: OCD is associated with an abnormality in which of the following parts of the brain?
questions.explanation: Basal ganglia dysfunction, particularly involving the caudate and lentiform nuclei, is implicated in obsessive-compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with respect to blood brain barrier?

options.text: Lipophilic substances penetrate the barrier better
Microglial foot processes form the blood brain barrier
Inflammation can strengthen blood brain barrier

correct_answer.text: Lipophilic substances penetrate the barrier better

correct_answers.text: Lipophilic substances penetrate the barrier better

questions.explanation: Lipophilic (fat-soluble) substances are able to more easily cross the blood-brain barrier due to their solubility in lipid membranes.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following cells is considered as descendants of macrophages that clear neuronal debris following cell death?
questions.explanation: Microglial cells are derived from yolk sac progenitors and act as the primary immune defense in the central nervous system, clearing cellular debris.

questions.question_text: The ventral tegmental area is located in which part of the brain?
questions.explanation: The ventral tegmental area (VTA) is part of the midbrain and is associated with the dopamine system, involved in reward and pleasure pathways.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with respect to cerebral dominance?

options.text: Most left handed individuals have bilateral dominance
Most left handed individuals have right cerebral dominance
Most left handed individuals have left cerebral dominance
Dominance cannot be ascertained in left handed individuals
Right handed individuals always have right cerebral dominance

correct_answer.text: Most left handed individuals have left cerebral dominance

correct_answers.text: Most left handed individuals have left cerebral dominance

questions.explanation: Most left-handed individuals (about 64%) have left hemisphere dominance, which is more common than right hemisphere dominance.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a function of oligodendrocytes?

options.text: Contributing to the blood brain barrier

questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes are responsible for myelination of axons in the central nervous system, providing insulation that facilitates rapid signal transmission.

questions.question_text: Neural crest cells originate from (AI chose ectoderm)
questions.explanation: Neural crest cells originate from the ectoderm, specifically from the dorsal part of the neural tube during embryogenesis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a purely motor cranial nerve?
questions.explanation: The oculomotor nerve is primarily a motor nerve controlling the majority of eye movements.

questions.question_text: Which area of the brain is associated with 'social valuation'?
questions.explanation: The orbitofrontal cortex plays a significant role in social valuation and decision making in social contexts.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is seen as a key function of the non-dominant cerebral hemisphere?
questions.explanation: The right hemisphere is generally better at processing visual-spatial information and pictorial memory.

questions.question_text: Primary sensory cortex is located in which of the following areas?
questions.explanation: The primary somatosensory cortex is located on the postcentral gyrus and is responsible for processing tactile information.

questions.question_text: Hippocampus is supplied by
questions.explanation: The hippocampus receives its blood supply primarily from the posterior cerebral artery.

questions.question_text: The motor cortex occupies
questions.explanation: The primary motor cortex is located in the precentral gyrus, which is responsible for initiating voluntary motor movements.

questions.question_text: Which part of the brain is last to mature?
questions.explanation: The prefrontal cortex is one of the last areas of the brain to mature during development.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cells are uniquely found in the cerebellum?
questions.explanation: Purkinje cells are a type of GABAergic neuron that are exclusively found in the cerebellar cortex.

questions.question_text: The most common type of neuronal cells seen in the cerebral cortex is
questions.explanation: Pyramidal neurons, characterized by their triangular-shaped cell bodies, constitute about 75% of the cortical neurons.

questions.question_text: What is the function of an endosome?

options.text: Check the synthesised proteins for structural conformity before delivery

questions.explanation: Endosomes are responsible for sorting and recycling cellular components, including membrane proteins.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following structures is a constituent of mesencephalon?
questions.explanation: The red nucleus is located within the mesencephalon (midbrain) and is involved in motor coordination.

questions.question_text: Electrical synapses are seen in
questions.explanation: Electrical synapses, which facilitate rapid communication between neurons, are notably present in the retina, among other locations.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following types of neuroglia is present in the peripheral nervous system?
questions.explanation: Schwann cells are the primary type of glial cells found in the peripheral nervous system, responsible for myelination.

questions.question_text: Which structure separates the two lateral ventricles in the human brain?
questions.explanation: The septum pellucidum is a membrane that separates the left and right lateral ventricles of the brain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following constitute the most common cells of the cerebral cortex?
questions.explanation: Stellate cells, which are present in all layers of the cerebral cortex except layer 1, are among the most common cell types.

questions.question_text: Huntington's disease is caused due to degeneration of
questions.explanation: Huntington's disease results from degeneration of the striatum, primarily affecting the caudate nucleus and leading to motor and cognitive symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following nuclei of basal ganglia contains melanin pigment?
questions.explanation: The substantia nigra appears darker due to the presence of melanin, which is a natural byproduct of dopamine synthesis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures give rise to cerebral hemispheres during embryogenesis?
questions.explanation: The telencephalon is the embryological structure that develops into the cerebral hemispheres.

questions.question_text: Which part of the brain is associated with aura in epilepsy?
questions.explanation: Auras are often linked to seizure activity in the temporal lobe, which may manifest as unusual sensations or experiences.

questions.question_text: Which lobe is initially affected in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease typically first impacts the temporal lobes, especially areas involved in memory, such as the hippocampus.

questions.question_text: A patient presents with rapid onset personality changes and memory difficulties. On examination, he has homonymous superior quadrantanopia. Where is the lesion likely to be?
questions.explanation: Homonymous superior quadrantanopia often results from lesions in the temporal lobe, especially affecting the optic radiation.

questions.question_text: Regarding the blood supply of language areas which of the following is correct?

options.text: Transient ischemia of carotid system produces aphasia
Right sided carotid block produces Broca's aphasia
Vertebrobasilar system supplies motor speech area
Wernicke's area is supplied by posterior cerebral artery
Transient ischemia of carotid system produces dysarthria

correct_answer.text: Transient ischemia of carotid system produces aphasia

correct_answers.text: Transient ischemia of carotid system produces aphasia

questions.explanation: Transient ischemia affecting the carotid system can lead to aphasia, as the areas responsible for language are supplied by it.

questions.question_text: Nucleus accumbens forms a part of which of the following structures of the brain?
questions.explanation: The nucleus accumbens is a key component of the ventral striatum, involved in the reward circuitry of the brain.
